independentRootCauseRederivation.method: Read lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/tools.ts (all 1004 lines) and lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/operative-state.ts (all 986 lines) / types.ts (all 369 lines) directly, before reading any of the implementer's own docs 01-12.
findings: resolveNodeWithSupersessionAwareness (tools.ts lines ~293-331) is the shared helper used by getParentClause, getSiblingClauses, getReferencedProvision (both its absolute-ref and fromNodeId/relative-ref resolution branches) - confirmed by direct call-site read, not assumed from the implementer's report.

getChildren does NOT call resolveNodeWithSupersessionAwareness - confirmed: it has its own dedicated resolveParentSubstructureEvidence (tools.ts lines ~363-379), which answers a genuinely different question (parent substructure validity) and, critically for this audit, NEVER branches on currentText null-ness at all - only on view.status directly (`viewBlocksTrust = view !== undefined && view.status !== "OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED"`). This structural difference is exactly why getChildren survives the fresh exploit variant found below while its 3 siblings do not.

The ORIGINAL OPEN-2 defect (view.currentText null discarding view.status entirely, falling back to raw node-level supersession) is genuinely fixed for the shapes the implementer's own matrix covers: CONFLICTED (already-effective and prospective), PARTIAL-via-ambiguous/unresolved-target, REVIEW_REQUIRED-via-effect.status-field-on-a-dated-effect, and clean deletion. Independently reproduced via 27 fresh, non-duplicated test cases in tests/certification/open2-terminal-independent-recert-fresh2.test.ts sections 1-9 (mixed applied+prospective chains, exact-boundary effective dates, genuinely ambiguous physical targets, the fromNodeId relative-reference code path, 3-sibling aggregate masking, and clean-deletion via getParentClause/getChildren) - all pass, all confirming the fix holds for those shapes.

STILL-OPEN RESIDUAL FOUND: resolveNodeWithSupersessionAwareness's own `if (view.currentText !== null && view.currentText !== undefined)` branch (tools.ts line ~298) is taken UNCONDITIONALLY whenever currentText is non-null - it never re-checks view.status inside that branch. The function's own header comment (tools.ts lines ~250-252) claims this is safe because 'by buildProvisionView's own invariant this only ever happens when view.status === OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED.' That claim is FALSE. buildProvisionView (operative-state.ts) only explicitly nulls currentText in 3 places: (a) inside the applied-chain loop, for a DELETE/no-newText effect, (b) the hasConflict branch, (c) the targetUnresolved||structuralHealthUnsafe branch. When a provision's status is OPERATIVE_STATE_REVIEW_REQUIRED PURELY because of an AMENDMENT_SEQUENCE_UNRESOLVED conflict (an effect with a genuinely unresolvable EffectiveDateResult - CONDITIONAL_UNRESOLVED or UNKNOWN, e.g. an amendment 'effective upon satisfaction of the Merger Condition, not yet obtained') and hasConflict/targetUnresolved/structuralHealthUnsafe are all false, NONE of the 3 explicit-null sites run for that effect (appliedChain's own filter is `e.effectiveDate.date !== null && ... <= asOfMs`, so an undated effect never enters the loop at all), so currentText is left as whatever it was before - the untouched base-document text (non-null) when this is the provision's only effect, or a real applied predecessor's own newText when a dated effect also applied earlier in the same chain. Either way, view.status is honestly REVIEW_REQUIRED, currentText is honestly non-null, and resolveNodeWithSupersessionAwareness reports evidenceCurrent:true - the exact class of defect (text-selection state silently gating trust-selection) OPEN-2 Part A was supposed to close in general, surviving in one specific, realistic corner it did not construct a test for.
